title: O1 – Introduction: what is an organisation?

blocks.text: An organisation is more than the sum of its members: the performance of an organisation of n individuals differs from the sum of the n individual performances.
Course definition: organisations consist in a stable collaboration of actors, following common general objectives through division of work and functions, and through specific coordination mechanisms.
Organisations matter: they play a major role in our societies, come in a variety of forms with advantages and drawbacks, and the right organisational choices are key for performance and success.
Organisations strongly affect individuals and influence their behaviour (Zimbardo's Stanford prison experiment, 1971).

Understanding the complexity of organisations is a key managerial competency: after their thirties, managers stand out by understanding complex organisational phenomena, not by technical skills (Audencia & Essec, 2014).

sections.heading: What is an organisation? Classic definitions

blocks.text: A set of social units essentially meant to reach specific objectives.
Open systems consisting of activities interwoven with individuals.
The rational coordination of activities of a number of people pursuing common goals, through a division of work and functions, hierarchy and responsibilities.
An answer to the problem of collective action.
A set of activity systems oriented toward an end and maintaining their frontiers.
A collective action in search of a common mission.
Stable collaboration of actors · common general objectives · division of work and functions · specific coordination mechanisms.
Students randomly assigned to be guards or prisoners quickly adopted abusive or submissive behaviour – the role and the setting, not personality, drove behaviour.

Two marginalised people were convicted of terrorism in 2015; in 2016 the Supreme Court of British Columbia overturned the verdict because the police had essentially created the plot. Class question: which organisational features (i) and mindsets (ii) led to this outcome, and what would you recommend to the RCMP?
Jérôme Kerviel (Société Générale) and Kenneth Lay (Enron): individual misconduct that the organisation made possible.
